chapter_title: Geometric Proofs, Circle Geometry, and Networks (10 & 10A)

worksheets.title: Deductive Geometric Proofs and Network Algorithms

fluency_questions.prompt: State the geometric reason that justifies each angle fact:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Two intersecting straight lines form equal opposite angles

parts.label: b
parts.question: A transversal crossing parallel lines forms equal Z-angles
parts.answer: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal

parts.label: c
parts.question: The three interior angles of any triangle add to $180^\circ$
parts.answer: Angle sum of a triangle is $180^\circ$

parts.label: d
parts.question: In $\triangle ABC$, if $AB = AC$, then $\angle B = \angle C$
parts.answer: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal

fluency_questions.prompt: A triangle network has $V = 3$ vertices ($A, B, C$) and $E = 3$ edges ($AB, BC, CA$). State:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The degree of vertex $A$ (number of edges meeting at $A$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: The sum of the degrees of all $3$ vertices ($2 + 2 + 2$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: The number of faces $F$ (1 inside face $+ 1$ outside face) and verify $V - E + F = 2$

parts.label: d
parts.question: The minimum number of edges needed to keep all $3$ vertices connected in a tree ($V - 1$)

fluency_questions.prompt: Count how many **odd-degree** vertices are in each list of vertex degrees:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Degrees: $2, 2, 2, 2$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Degrees: $3, 2, 3, 2$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Degrees: $1, 2, 1$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Degrees: $3, 3, 3, 3$

fluency_questions.prompt: In a small town network, the road from $A$ to $B$ is $5\text{ km}$, from $B$ to $C$ is $4\text{ km}$, and the direct road from $A$ to $C$ is $11\text{ km}$. Find:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The distance from $A$ to $C$ via $B$ ($A \to B \to C$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Which route from $A$ to $C$ is shorter: direct ($11\text{ km}$) or via $B$ ($9\text{ km}$)?

parts.label: c
parts.question: How many kilometres are saved by taking the shorter path

parts.label: d
parts.question: The total length of the Minimum Spanning Tree using the two shortest roads ($4\text{ km}$ and $5\text{ km}$)

application_questions.question: A planar map of park paths has $V = 4$ junctions and $E = 6$ paths. Use Euler's formula $V - E + F = 2$ (so $4 - 6 + F = 2$) to find the number of regions (faces) $F$.

A postman wants to walk along every street in a network once without repeating any street. The network has exactly $2$ odd-degree corners ($A$ and $B$) and all other corners have even degree. Where must the postman start and finish?
application_questions.answer: Start at one odd corner ($A$) and finish at the other odd corner ($B$).

application_questions.question: A park council wants to lay water pipes to connect $4$ drinking fountains ($V = 4$) using a spanning tree. How many pipe segments ($V - 1$) are required?
In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $AC$. By the Midpoint Theorem, $DE$ is half the length of base $BC$. If $BC = 18\text{ cm}$, find the length of $DE$.

reasoning_questions.question: In a deductive geometry proof, why is measuring angles with a protractor on a diagram NOT accepted as a mathematical proof?
reasoning_questions.answer: Measurements on a single drawing are only approximate and apply only to that one specific drawing, whereas a deductive proof uses geometric laws to prove the result holds exactly for all possible cases.

reasoning_questions.question: Why does a **spanning tree** never contain a closed loop (cycle)?
reasoning_questions.answer: If a network had a closed loop, you could remove one edge from the loop and all vertices would still remain connected with less total weight.

worksheets.title: [10A] Circle Geometry: Angle, Chord, and Tangent Theorems

fluency_questions.prompt: The angle at the centre of a circle is **twice** the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc. Find the missing angle:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Angle at circumference $= 30^\circ$; find angle at the centre ($2 \times 30^\circ$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Angle at circumference $= 45^\circ$; find angle at the centre ($2 \times 45^\circ$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Angle at the centre $= 100^\circ$; find angle at the circumference ($100^\circ \div 2$)

parts.label: d
parts.question: Angle at the centre $= 140^\circ$; find angle at the circumference ($140^\circ \div 2$)

fluency_questions.prompt: Use the semicircle rule (angle in a semicircle $= 90^\circ$) and the same-segment rule (angles in the same segment are equal) to find $x^\circ$:

parts.label: a
parts.question: $AB$ is a diameter and $C$ is on the circle; state $\angle ACB = x^\circ$

parts.label: b
parts.question: In $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$ and $\angle CAB = 40^\circ$, find $\angle ABC = x^\circ$

parts.label: c
parts.question: $\angle ACB$ and $\angle ADB$ stand on the same arc $AB$. If $\angle ACB = 35^\circ$, find $\angle ADB = x^\circ$

parts.label: d
parts.question: $\angle PRQ$ and $\angle PSQ$ stand on the same arc $PQ$. If $\angle PRQ = 62^\circ$, find $\angle PSQ = x^\circ$

fluency_questions.prompt: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to $180^\circ$. Find the opposite angle $x^\circ$:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Given angle $= 80^\circ$; find $x = 180 - 80$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Given angle $= 110^\circ$; find $x = 180 - 110$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Given angle $= 95^\circ$; find $x = 180 - 95$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Given angle $= 64^\circ$; find $x = 180 - 64$

fluency_questions.prompt: Use tangent properties (a tangent meets a radius at $90^\circ$, and two tangents from an external point $P$ have equal length $PA = PB$):

parts.label: a
parts.question: Radius $OT$ meets tangent $PT$ at $T$; state the size of $\angle OTP$

parts.label: b
parts.question: If tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn from $P$ and $PA = 12\text{ cm}$, find the length of $PB$

parts.label: c
parts.question: In right-angled $\triangle OTP$ ($\angle OTP = 90^\circ$), if $OT = 3\text{ cm}$ and $PT = 4\text{ cm}$, find $OP$

parts.label: d
parts.question: If $\angle OTP = 90^\circ$ and $\angle TOP = 60^\circ$, find $\angle OPT$

application_questions.question: A circular walking track has a straight bridge $AB$ passing right through the centre $O$ (so $AB$ is a diameter). A kiosk $C$ sits on the edge of the circle. What is the size of $\angle ACB$?
Four picnic tables $A, B, C, D$ sit on the edge of a circular plaza, forming a cyclic quadrilateral. If the angle at table $A$ is $75^\circ$, what is the angle at the opposite table $C$?

A bicycle wheel of radius $r = 30\text{ cm}$ rests on flat horizontal ground (which acts as a tangent to the wheel at the contact point $T$). What angle does the vertical radius $OT$ make with the ground?
Two intersecting chords $AB$ and $CD$ cross at $P$ inside a circle. Using $AP \times PB = CP \times PD$, find $PD$ if $AP = 2\text{ cm}$, $PB = 6\text{ cm}$, and $CP = 3\text{ cm}$.

reasoning_questions.question: How can you quickly check whether a four-sided shape $ABCD$ can have a circle drawn through all four of its corners (a cyclic quadrilateral)?
reasoning_questions.answer: Check whether its opposite interior angles add up to $180^\circ$ ($\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ$ and $\angle B + \angle D = 180^\circ$).

reasoning_questions.question: Why is any triangle formed by two radii $OA$ and $OB$ and a chord $AB$ inside a circle always an **isosceles** triangle?
reasoning_questions.answer: Because $OA$ and $OB$ are both radii of the same circle, so they have equal length ($OA = OB$).
